pairs: Quis mihi det te fratrem meum,
Bride to Groom: Who will give you to me as my brother,
feeding from the breasts of my mother,
so that I may discover you outside,
and so that now no one may despise me?
I will take hold of you
et ducam in domum matris meæ:
and lead you into my mother’s house.
et dabo tibi poculum ex vino condito,
and I will give you a cup of spiced wine,
and of new wine from my pomegranates.
His left hand is under my head,
and his right hand shall embrace me.
not to disturb or awaken the beloved,
Quæ est ista quæ ascendit de deserto,
Chorus to Groom: Who is she,
deliciis affluens, innixa super dilectum suum?
ibi corrupta est mater tua, ibi violata est genitrix tua.
Pone me ut signaculum super cor tuum,
quia fortis est ut mors dilectio,
lampades ejus lampades ignis atque flammarum.
There she who bore you was violated.
Aquæ multæ non potuerunt extinguere caritatem,
Set me like a seal upon your heart,
like a seal upon your arm.
Si dederit homo omnem substantiam domus suæ pro dilectione,
For love is strong, like death, and envy is enduring,
like hell: their lamps are made of fire and flames.
Soror nostra parva, et ubera non habet;
A multitude of waters cannot extinguish love, nor can a river overwhelm it.
quid faciemus sorori nostræ in die quando alloquenda est?
If a man were to give all the substance of his house in exchange for love, he would despise it as nothing.
What shall we do for our sister on the day when she is called upon?
let us build a rampart of silver upon it.
ex quo facta sum coram eo,
let us join it together with boards of cedar.
Vinea fuit pacifico in ea quæ habet populos:
Bride to Chorus: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers,
vir affert pro fructu ejus mille argenteos.
I have become like one who has discovered peace.
The peaceful one had a vineyard, in that which held the peoples.
He handed it on to the caretakers;
et ducenti his qui custodiunt fructus ejus.
a man brought, in exchange for its fruit, a thousand pieces of silver.
Groom: My vineyard is before me.
The thousand is for your peacefulness,
and two hundred is for those who care for its fruit.
Your friends are attentive to those who have been dwelling in the gardens. Cause me to heed your voice.
Flee away, my beloved, and become like the doe and the young stag upon the mountains of aromatic plants.
